messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: high error rate and latency spike observed for tenant 'AcmeCorp' in VPC-dedicated pool dp-us-east-2-03. Alert rule: kv_prefix_hitrate < 5% for 5m (severity: paging).

maria: saw this on the dashboard 18:12 UTC. KV prefix hit rate crashed from ~78% to 2% for AcmeCorp. Tail latency for text generation jumped to ~1.2s p50 -> 2.8s p99, and per-token cost spiked. Looks tenant-specific (other tenants in same pool fine). :eyes:

sam: confirming. Correlation with a large tenant rollout? Any recent model or config change for AcmeCorp? I see a config push to their dedicated pool ~17:50 (quantization tweaks) but nothing touching cache config.

leo: logs show a flood of unique prefix keys from that tenant starting 17:48 — suspicious pattern: prefix key churn. Might be client-side instantiating many ephemeral prefixes (bad prompt engineering). Sample query stream:

```
# kibana query
index=kv-ops tenant=acmecorp AND timestamp:["2026-03-15T17:45:00" TO "2026-03-15T18:15:00"] | stats count by prefix_key
```

Many one-off prefixes with low reuse.

anya: customer-ops says they rolled out a new feature that includes user-specific conversation ids in prompts. Could be generating near-infinitely unique prefixes. They didn't intend to change caching behavior.

gavin: mitigation idea: disable prefix-level caching for that tenant immediately to stop pollution and fallback to per-request KV usage. That should stop cache thrashing and isolate other tenants. We can enable with runtime flag `TENANT_CACHE_MODE=disabled` scoped to AcmeCorp.

maria: agree. I'm going to apply a scoped override to disable prefix caching for AcmeCorp and also set a temporary TTL=1s cleanup window. Applying now.

maria: applied override via control plane: `PATCH /v1/pools/dp-us-east-2-03/tenants/acmecorp/config` payload:

```
{ "kv_cache": { "prefix_cache_enabled": false, "prefix_ttl_seconds": 1 } }
```

sam: rolling a change on serving nodes in that pool to pick up config. Watch logs for error spikes.

incident-bot: Deploy task 4321 started by maria. Canary: 10% nodes.

leo: canary looks clean for 2 minutes. Hitrate for other tenants stable. AcmeCorp hit-rate now reported as 0% (expected when disabled) but latency is dropping p99 -> 1.0s within 3 minutes. Good.

kevin: we should also purge polluted keys in the tenant KV namespace so the cache warmers don't keep thrashing when re-enabled. Running a targeted purge job (dry-run first):

```
# purge job
POST /internal/kv/purge
{ "tenant":"acmecorp","pattern":"prefix_*","max_keys":100000 }
```

Dry-run shows ~84k candidate keys created since 17:45.

anya: customer contact: AcmeCorp SE notified, they acknowledge the client-side change. Asking for ETA to re-enable once we confirm stable. Posting recommended client fix: stop baking ephemeral convo ids into prompt-key prefixes; use stable session id.

gavin: next steps: 1) keep tenant cache disabled, 2) run purge, 3) contact infra to lift burst capacity if any remaining backlog, 4) prepare rollback plan to re-enable with warmup TTL/limit. Assigning tasks.

maria: handoff to oncall-sre for overnight monitoring. @sam please follow up with a postmortem once metrics settle.

sam: taking oncall handoff. I'll add a timeline and root-cause notes in incidents channel. Initial RCA: client-induced prefix key explosion causing tenant-level cache pollution -> hit-rate collapse -> increased backend load and latency. Suggested persistent fix: add server-side guardrails (rate-limit new prefix creation per tenant) and admin knob for immediate eviction.

account-ps: I'll coordinate customer comms and a short RCA summary for AcmeCorp execs. Also cc legal if they request logs.

customer-ops: confirm purge started at 18:30 UTC. Monitoring keyspace and backend error queue. We'll update when purge completes (~eta 20min).

leo: after purge, consider re-enabling prefix cache with a staged warmup: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% and TTL back to 300s, plus server-side cap: `max_new_prefixes_per_minute=50`.

sam: noted. I'll add the server-side cap RFC ticket and mark as P1. Anything else? :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone. Postmortem tag: acmecorp-kv-prefix-20260315. Leaving thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
